newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL money market closed for Moslem festival.
newsitem.headline: KL money market closed for Moslem festival.

text.p: The Malaysian money market and interest rate futures bourse, the Malaysia Monetary Exchange, are closed on Friday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha celebrations.
The markets will reopen on Monday with interest rates expected to rise further due to liquidity shortages.
Dealers said fresh outflow of funds from the banking system, mainly through foreign funds leaving Malaysia, was expected to tighten the market further next week.
On Thursday, the overnight rate ended at 8.4/6 percent.
Dealers said with Bank Negara announcing plans to roll over a maturing 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill next Wednesday, the market was expected to remain tight.
One-week money ended the week at 8.10/20 percent against 7.80/90 percent on Wednesday, while two-week was at 7.50/60 percent and three-week at 7.35/40 percent.
One-month to six-month money traded between 7.35 and 7.45 percent and nine-month and one-year rose to 7.45/48 percent against 7.40/45, the dealers said.
The market tightened on Wednesday after an outflow of 500 million ringgit due to a Bank Negara bill.
The outflow coupled with a steady draining of foreign funds from Malaysia had tightened the market and pushed up rates, dealers said.
Dealers said there was market talk that foreign funds were withdrawing from Malaysia, both from deposits and from the stock market, which has been falling sharply recently.

Last week, Bank Negara intervened to slow the ringgit's fall by selling nearly $200 million, dealers said. A 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue also reduced liquidity in the flush market. -- Madhav Reddy (603-230 7509) .
